answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with liveness-bound stake escrow. Each identity locks a deposit in a harbor contract and must periodically answer unpredictable puzzles tied to its key; missing one slashes the deposit. Old credentials become a relic: past work earns no permanent trust, only a decaying score, so an attacker cannot buy or farm one good history and clone it. The delta between honest upkeep and Sybil farming is the cost: every fake identity pays the same recurring compute and capital lockup, so a thousand fakes cost a thousandfold, while honest agents pay once.
